From 80e9963fb3b5509dfcabe9652d56bf4b35542055 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nianyao Tang <tangnianyao@huawei.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Apr 2024 02:27:37 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] irqchip/gic-v3-its: Fix VSYNC referencing an unmapped VPE on
 GIC v4.1

As per the GICv4.1 spec (Arm IHI 0069H, 5.3.19):

 "A VMAPP with {V, Alloc}=={0, x} is self-synchronizing, This means the ITS
  command queue does not show the command as consumed until all of its
  effects are completed."

Furthermore, VSYNC is allowed to deliver an SError when referencing a
non existent VPE.

By these definitions, a VMAPP followed by a VSYNC is a bug, as the
later references a VPE that has been unmapped by the former.

Fix it by eliding the VSYNC in this scenario.

Fixes: 64edfaa9a234 ("irqchip/gic-v4.1: Implement the v4.1 flavour of VMAPP")
Signed-off-by: Nianyao Tang <tangnianyao@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Reviewed-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Zenghui Yu <yuzenghui@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240406022737.3898763-1-tangnianyao@huawei.com

diff --git a/drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3-its.c b/drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3-its.c
index fca888b36680..2a537cbfcb07 100644
--- a/drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3-its.c
+++ b/drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3-its.c
@@ -786,6 +786,7 @@ static struct its_vpe *its_build_vmapp_cmd(struct its_node *its,
 					   struct its_cmd_block *cmd,
 					   struct its_cmd_desc *desc)
 {
+	struct its_vpe *vpe = valid_vpe(its, desc->its_vmapp_cmd.vpe);
 	unsigned long vpt_addr, vconf_addr;
 	u64 target;
 	bool alloc;
@@ -798,6 +799,11 @@ static struct its_vpe *its_build_vmapp_cmd(struct its_node *its,
 		if (is_v4_1(its)) {
 			alloc = !atomic_dec_return(&desc->its_vmapp_cmd.vpe->vmapp_count);
 			its_encode_alloc(cmd, alloc);
+			/*
+			 * Unmapping a VPE is self-synchronizing on GICv4.1,
+			 * no need to issue a VSYNC.
+			 */
+			vpe = NULL;
 		}
 
 		goto out;
@@ -832,7 +838,7 @@ static struct its_vpe *its_build_vmapp_cmd(struct its_node *its,
 out:
 	its_fixup_cmd(cmd);
 
-	return valid_vpe(its, desc->its_vmapp_cmd.vpe);
+	return vpe;
 }
 
 static struct its_vpe *its_build_vmapti_cmd(struct its_node *its,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/irqchip/irq-gic-v3-its.c`**
   - A new variable `vpe` is introduced to hold the result of the `valid_vpe` function call.
   - A comment is added to clarify that unmapping a VPE is self-synchronizing on GICv4.1, indicating that a VSYNC does not need to be issued in this case.
   - The return statement at the end of the `its_build_vmapp_cmd` function is modified to return the `vpe` variable instead of calling `valid_vpe` again.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `irq-gic-v3-its.c` file are directly related to the bug fix described in the patch. The change addresses the issue where a VSYNC command was incorrectly issued after a VMAPP command that unmapped a VPE. By introducing the `vpe` variable and setting it to `NULL` when a VPE is unmapped, the code ensures that the VSYNC is not issued in this scenario, thus adhering to the GICv4.1 specification and preventing potential errors related to referencing an unmapped VPE. This change effectively resolves the bug identified in the previous implementation.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
its_encode_cmd(cmd, GITS_CMD_VMAPP);
its_encode_vpeid(cmd, desc->its_vmapp_cmd.vpe->vpe_id);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the VSYNC command is issued after the VMAPP command, which unmapped a Virtual Processing Element (VPE). According to the GICv4.1 specification, the effects of the VMAPP command are not finalized until all its effects are completed. Therefore, when the VSYNC command references the VPE that has just been unmapped, it leads to an SError due to referencing a non-existent VPE.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
vpe = NULL;
goto out;
```
Reason:
The fix involves setting the `vpe` variable to `NULL` and skipping the issuance of the VSYNC command when a VPE is unmapped. This prevents the VSYNC from referencing a VPE that no longer exists, thus adhering to the self-synchronizing behavior defined in the GICv4.1 specification and avoiding the potential SError.
